dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Cluster = 17 rows, term_days=365, posted 31 May 21:03–21:46, effective 01–28 May | recharges.csv"
"All 42 files tie exactly: 90 received = 90 accepted, cash = ledger, recon diff $0.00, 0 duplicate source events | log vs recharges"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Lag >0 occurs only for term_days=365, only for these 2 dealers, only from March; Jan–Feb same-day; all other channels lag 0 always"
"Pipeline defect — rejected as stated. Batching is deliberate and began cleanly at 2026-03-31; every file reconciles. It is a design consequence, not a failure."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Entitlement posting is unevidenced. The email names four DealerDrop checks; the log has columns for only three. No entitlement field exists for the 90 batched rows."
"Would change my decision: entitlement records showing service start keyed to posted_at rather than effective_event_date (→ customer harm, escalate)"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Rebuild the weekly trend pack on effective_event_date, keeping posted_at only as a lag metric"
"All read-only — no ledger changes, no dealer contact, fully reversible."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not escalate as duplicate or manipulated revenue."
"Escalate instead, at low severity, as (a) a trend-pack methodology defect on our side and (b) two unverified controls."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The 31 May cluster is a fully reconciled month-end batch-posting artifact" overstates the evidence because entitlement posting for the 90 batched rows is explicitly unevidenced and the ledger total is self-reported within the same log.
"No revenue is duplicated" is well supported for recharge IDs, source events, cash, and the supplied ledger fields, but is stronger than warranted until entitlement records are checked independently.
"Batching is deliberate" is a plausible causal inference from the consistent dealer-specific pattern, but the supplied data establishes the pattern more directly than the intent.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative is an entitlement or service-start defect: the cash and recharge records can reconcile while downstream entitlement posting is duplicated or keyed to posted_at rather than effective_event_date. The analyst handled this reasonably by identifying the missing entitlement evidence and specifying escalation triggers, but the headline conclusion could have qualified the no-duplicate-revenue claim more narrowly.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Rephrase the headline conclusion to distinguish what is proven from what remains unknown: no evidence of duplicate cash or duplicate recharge events, but no final entitlement conclusion until the 90-row entitlement/GL extracts are independently reconciled.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell 38.4% after the 10 May cutover (6.12 to 3.77 cases/day) while N (+1.8%), E (-3.2%) and W (+16.4%) were flat or rising over identical 52/51-day windows."
"650 of 2,709 NovaIVR sessions (24.0%) terminate at the authenticate stage, 464 of them abandoned or errored, and by Farah's own email these sit outside CareDesk case reporting."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Three facts break the improvement story: (1) South fault load rose, not fell ... yet NO_SIGNAL cases halved ..."
"Legacy IVR logging is not comparable to Nova ... legacy records contain zero pre-auth abandonments — almost certainly a logging gap rather than a real zero."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Suppressed reporting, not reduced dissatisfaction, is the primary driver of the decline" ... "Confidence: Medium-High (causal claim)"
"Material unknowns: ... Whether case-creation rules or entitlements changed at cutover ... What outcome RESOLVED means ... Telephony data is absent entirely."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally."
"Hold the pilot at current South scope (neither expand nor roll back) and pull the CareDesk change log for the week of 10 May to test the non-IVR channel drop."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Expansion is reconsidered only after the corrected rate is stable for two full weeks and the TOKEN_MISMATCH and ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT defects are closed."
"Show me the exact CareDesk case-creation rule in force on 9 May versus 11 May ... was the rule, intake form, or entitlement check changed for DEALER and APP origin cases on either date?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that "Suppressed reporting, not reduced dissatisfaction, is the primary driver of the decline" is stronger than the evidence establishes; the evidence supports missing case creation as a leading explanation, not proof that dissatisfaction did not also change.
The claim that Farah is "the only person who can supply" the needed definitions and records is unsupported and unnecessarily absolute.

The stated "49.3% served on the full funnel of all 2,709 offered sessions" is not reproducible from the figures shown and uses an unclear definition of served; the submission should show the numerator and denominator explicitly.

The proposed requirement that TOKEN_MISMATCH and ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT defects be "closed" and that the corrected rate be stable for "two full weeks" is operationally reasonable but not justified by an explicit decision threshold or power/variance assessment.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately handles genuine service improvement, seasonality or national trends, and genuine IVR deflection as alternatives, and it preserves the possibility of a CareDesk rule or entitlement change. The main remaining alternative is an administrative, taxonomy, or origin-attribution change affecting Dealer and App cases independently of IVR, which the requested CareDesk change-log review would test; it is not yet resolved by the observed service-event and IVR evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reconcile every funnel metric with an explicit numerator, denominator, and eligibility rule, especially the claimed 49.3% full-funnel result, then link offered sessions, authentication outcomes, case creation, repeat contacts, and sampled calls at the journey level before making the causal claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies `inverter_events.csv`, enumerates all four rows, and cites specific fields such as `impact_mw`, `cleared`, duration, inverter ID, severity, and event name.
It distinguishes observation from inference, stating high confidence that the originating event is absent but low confidence about whether this reflects the window boundary or an extraction filter.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks the apparent burst/gap against inverter identity and recurrence: “the four events fall on four different inverters ... with no unit recurring.”
It tests an innocent explanation—filtered or incomplete extraction—rather than treating the six-day gap as evidence of a plant problem.
Reasoning is necessarily based on one event-export channel and does not fully verify event semantics or the underlying source records.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table gives claim-specific confidence, including “Low as to why” the originating event is absent and “Low for what they imply about plant state.”
The submission explicitly avoids claiming that four rows establish plant health and states that constant zero `impact_mw` cannot independently validate the no-impact interpretation.
It limits the conclusion to a cheap extraction-scope check and then stopping.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Perform one cheap check, then stop” is proportionate to four cleared events, durations of 1–7 minutes, zero reported MW impact, and no repeated inverter.

Requesting the extraction query or filter, including predicates on severity, event type, date, and inverter set, is a discriminating next check that could explain the missing originating event and the apparent quiet period.
“Do not escalate” preserves operational proportionality while leaving room for the stated scope check.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the supplied dynamics: it does not invent a plant problem from a short communications warning, notes zero reported MW impact and quick clearing, and stops after a low-cost quality check.
It appropriately treats the event naming as insufficient evidence: “the one `warning`-severity row is a single 7-minute comms event whose name is not by itself evidence of a comms problem.”

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Every downstream rate or trend claim depends on knowing the filter” is broader than necessary; some descriptive rates within the exported file remain valid even if the export is filtered, provided they are scoped to the file.

The statement that asking for the filter “resolves Finding 1 and the rejected hypothesis at once” is slightly overstated: the originating event could still predate the window or be absent from the underlying source, even with a known filter.

The submission says the file is “simply a quiet nine days” if unrestricted; that is reasonable as a description of this export but should not be generalized to plant-wide behavior without confirming source completeness.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be incomplete or filtered, so the apparent 27–29 May burst and six-day gap may describe extraction behavior rather than plant behavior. If the query is unrestricted and the source is complete, the alternative interpretation is an ordinary, low-impact set of transient events rather than a developing multi-unit fault.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: After obtaining the extraction predicate, verify the event-pairing and date-boundary semantics against the underlying event source—especially whether the INV-09 recovery has a preceding fault outside the window—so the missing-origin observation is converted into a tested explanation rather than only a scope hypothesis.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies specific inputs such as “base_schedule_mw vs submitted_schedule_mw,” “identical actual_mw,” “dispatch_blocks.csv,” and DSM rate bands, and gives reproducible values for the 29 May comparison.
It distinguishes the note’s “Generation gap” from recomputed absolute block deviations and identifies the affected blocks, times, ratios, gust ranges, and penalties.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests the central causal comparison by noting that “31.6% figure is ... a between-day difference between two dates, not a treatment effect.”
It triangulates block-level schedule changes, metered generation, wind, stow state, DSM bands, untreated-day penalties, and firmware differences rather than relying on the headline figure.
The claim that the pilot used a “uniform 3.865% haircut” and that blocks 63–64 worsened is a concrete mechanism test, not merely anomaly spotting.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly says the 31.6% figure is “causally unsupported” and identifies missing submission timestamps, uncertainty about ex-ante timing, and uncertainty about revenue caps.
It appropriately qualifies June comparisons because “June days ran firmware 4.8.”

However, calling the 17.6% result “the pilot’s defensible effect” and saying the “remaining ~14 points ... are day-to-day variation” overstates what the same-day accounting counterfactual identifies: it supports a schedule-replacement estimate, not necessarily a causal pilot effect, and the exact decomposition of the 31.6 points is not established.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to continue in “shadow mode only,” retain “qca_base” for settlement, and avoid external citation of 31.6% is reversible and preserves operational constraints.
The proposed pre-registered paired design compares the pilot against a fixed 3.87% haircut and requires gate timestamps, directly testing whether wind logic adds value beyond under-scheduling.
The recommendation also recognizes the unresolved settlement issue by discussing the 7.63 MWh above-schedule delivery and potential revenue consequences.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion preserves the smaller same-day benefit instead of claiming “no value,” while correctly rejecting the headline as a controlled causal estimate.
The statement that the pilot’s demonstrated mechanism is “schedule reduction,” rather than proven generation improvement or wind-aware optimization, is well aligned with the supplied evidence.
The qualification that the result is based on a same-day counterfactual is substantially more defensible than treating the 31.6% between-day comparison as causal.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The pilot’s defensible effect” and “17.6% same-day effect” are phrased causally even though the alternative schedule was not actually submitted and settled; the evidence establishes a modeled schedule-counterfactual saving under fixed-generation assumptions.
“The remaining ~14 points of the headline number are day-to-day variation” is directionally plausible but not quantitatively identified by the presented comparisons.

“The 34.6 MWh generation difference is weather” is stronger than the evidence warrants; similar gust maxima, stow counts, and high correlation support an innocent weather explanation but do not prove it.
“Reversible, costs nothing” is an operational assertion without evidence about the cost of shadow logging or process changes.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.6% figure may be entirely an accounting benefit from choosing a lower submitted schedule, not evidence that the pilot’s wind or tracker logic improved performance. It could also be offset or dominated by lost energy revenue if settlement is capped at the accepted schedule. The pilot may therefore have demonstrated a potentially useful under-scheduling policy, while still providing no evidence that its claimed adaptive mechanism adds value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain authoritative settlement treatment and timestamped pre-gate submissions for a paired pilot-versus-fixed-haircut test. This would determine both whether the 17.6% accounting saving is economically real and whether the pilot adds causal value beyond a flat 3.87% schedule reduction.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declaration line 1 declares P1001 under 90211000..." sourced to "declaration.pdf"
"Swiss approved code for P1001 is 90211000, effective 2025-01-01, no end date" sourced to "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Swiss Matrix row 0"
"Helios code 90211090 equals the current EU CN8 row for P1001 in DE, FR and BE effective 2025-07-01" sourced to "product_master_current.xlsx vs EU Matrix"
"Product master is a 2025-12-31 snapshot with no effective-dated history, so it post-dates and cannot validate a 2025-11-04 filing"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Do not escalate as a declaration error. Close the flag as a false positive arising from a cross-nomenclature comparison"
"The automated comparator compared a Swiss local code against an EU-derived commercial code and reported the expected difference as a defect"
"Separately, and not part of the flag: the commercial invoice does not foot"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "High (observed)" and "High (documented)" confidence labels distinguish direct observations from documentation
"Product master is a 2025-12-31 snapshot with no effective-dated history, so it post-dates and cannot validate a 2025-11-04 filing"
"Helios is commercial master data; record status is not customs-ruling status"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The country matrix Read Me states that EU entries use CN8, Switzerland uses a Swiss local tariff code, and that matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected"
"Helios eight-character codes were populated by migration mapping where no local approved code was supplied"
"Canonical schema v0.3 does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version or effective dates"
"The root cause is visible in canonical-schema-v0.3.md"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate as a declaration error"
"log it as a control defect rather than a filing defect"
"the commercial invoice does not foot... should be routed to valuation review"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The automated comparator compared a Swiss local code against an EU-derived commercial code" is a plausible root-cause inference, but the submission does not cite a comparator log or rule showing exactly how the comparison was performed.
"The root cause is visible in canonical-schema-v0.3.md" is somewhat stronger than the evidence: the schema omission explains a capability gap but does not alone prove it caused this specific alert.
"This is a materially larger exposure" is directionally supported by the arithmetic, but the submission does not quantify the resulting duty, tax, or financial exposure.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The declaration code appears valid under the Swiss matrix, but the conclusion would be less secure if the matrix row were not authoritative for the relevant transaction or if an independent Swiss tariff validation identified a more specific code. The cited cross-nomenclature and date evidence makes that alternative weaker; the main remaining gap is direct evidence of the comparator rule or alert trace.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Attach the comparator alert/rule trace and retain an auditable calculation or source for the valuation discrepancy, while documenting that the declaration was validated against the authoritative Swiss code system and filing-date version.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declaration asserts Preference = Yes with Declared origin = United States..." tied to "declaration.pdf, line 1".
"P1006 appears in the register under five suppliers with five different origins" tied to "supplier_origin_register.csv".
The submission explicitly limits the supplier inference: "Low that SUP-02 is the actual supplier — nothing states this" and identifies the missing join evidence.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission tests and rejects multiple alternatives, including "Linking SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025 would resolve the flag," "SUP-02's expired declaration is the defect; renew it," and "Fall back to ERP origin where the document is blank."
It correctly distinguishes manufacturing evidence from preference evidence: "It attests manufacturing origin only."
It does not treat the ClearView null result as dispositive, stating: "Absence in ClearView is not absence of a document."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The submission appropriately qualifies the supplier inference: "High that the row explains the null result; Low that SUP-02 is the actual supplier — nothing states this."
It identifies precise gaps: "The supplier identity for this consignment" and "The preference code / legal basis the broker used."

Calibration is weakened by the categorical statement: "it cannot be supported by any evidence currently in the packet or the register," despite the acknowledged uncertainty about supplier identity and the possibility of a preferential-origin instrument not included in the current extract.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the data-lineage problem: "The register cannot be joined to this packet" because "no SUP-xx identifier appears anywhere."

It recognizes system limitations: Procurement says the register "is not always updated when sourcing routes change," and the response explains that a ClearView null result "does not prove that no document exists outside the register."
It connects policy and system behavior by noting the ERP fallback was "fine for extraction testing, not for clearing a preference claim."
The process explanation would be stronger with a sourced explanation of the applicable legal basis for the asserted EU/US conclusion.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The safe part of the recommendation is: "Do not close the ClearView flag by linking a supplier declaration" and the request for "supplier's declaration for preferential origin, naming an agreement and originating rule."
However, the proposed immediate action — "initiate a declaration amendment" — is stronger than the evidence supports while the supplier identity and broker preference code remain unknown.

The response also states "Two independent grounds, either sufficient on its own," although one ground is based largely on the absence of a document type in the current scope and the other relies on an uncited legal conclusion.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The preferential-origin claim ... cannot be supported by any evidence currently in the packet or the register" is overstated because the submission itself acknowledges that the packet cannot identify the supplier and that documents may exist outside the register; the defensible conclusion is that the claim is presently unsubstantiated.

"There is no EU preferential arrangement with the US under which US-originating goods receive preferential tariff treatment" may be legally correct in the relevant general sense, but it is asserted without a cited legal source or the broker's preference code, and therefore is not fully supported by the submission's evidence record.
"initiate a declaration amendment" is premature without first obtaining the supplier identity, broker legal basis, and preferential-origin evidence.

"The likely revenue impact is nil" is supported only by the current declaration's 0.0% duty and EUR 0.00 duty fields; it does not establish that no potential duty or other financial exposure exists if the declaration is corrected.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The claim is unresolved rather than disproven: the packet lacks the supplier identity and preference code, and the register is known to lag sourcing changes. A current or external supplier-specific preferential-origin declaration, or a valid legal basis under an agreement not shown in the extract, could change the conclusion. The available SUP-01 record supports only manufacturing origin and therefore cannot by itself validate preference.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the immediate amendment recommendation with a controlled hold-and-verify sequence: obtain the PO/ASN/goods receipt and broker preference code, identify the actual supplier, then obtain and test a supplier declaration that names the agreement and originating rule before deciding whether amendment is required.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 220 non-null qcore_release_ts values (84%) have time-of-day exactly 02:10:00" — specific field, count, and comparison to source_freshness.csv.
"All 42 HOLD rows are exactly the 42 batches received after 2026-07-22" and "No release timestamp anywhere exceeds 2026-07-22 02:10" — precise cross-tabs and temporal checks.
"Ops's ~36 h matches receipt→release... On the SOP basis... median is 17.9 h" — triangulates operational and SOP-defined intervals while acknowledging timestamp contamination.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The apparent cycle time... cannot be used as a KPI" is supported by the 02:10 concentration, stale-feed cutoff, and differing source snapshots.
"Stamp type drives the answer" distinguishes a possible interface/load-timestamp mechanism from the observed cycle-time symptom.
"A quality state would scatter across the 5-week receipt range; this is right-censoring by a stale feed" tests the competing explanation for HOLD status against the temporal pattern.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The table distinguishes confidence in the pattern from confidence in its interpretation: "High that the pattern exists; Medium that these are load stamps rather than a real 02:10 batch-disposition run."
The submission states the SOP-basis arithmetic is "Low as a true estimate" because it relies on contaminated stamps and requests confirmation of the ETL filler value.
Some conclusions are stronger than the evidence warrants, including that one catalog lookup "decides whether any cycle-time metric is recoverable at all."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Reframe the ask" correctly separates receipt→release from the SOP's required-evidence-available→disposition target.
"Until item 1 is answered, publish exception rates and volumes — not cycle time" is a reversible, risk-protective action.

The recommendation preserves useful analysis rather than declaring the entire extract worthless: "usable for volume, mix, and exception rates; it is specifically the disposition timestamp that fails."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission actively rejects the strongest alternative for HOLDs using the perfect temporal mapping and absence of corresponding quality indicators.
It rejects interpreting INDEX_PENDING as a control failure by distinguishing CertVault index timing from certificate availability and citing the portal's closer-to-real-time status.
It identifies what evidence could revive the timestamp interpretation: the catalog definition, a genuine event-timestamp extract, and confirmation of the filler value.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The primary request is narrowly scoped: "obtain the data catalog definition of qcore_release_ts... whether it records the disposition event or the QCore load."
The prioritized follow-ups target distinct uncertainties: a fresh QCore extract, the site exception log, and confirmation of the ETL fill value.
The requested evidence is tied to decision impact: salvage the metric if it is an event timestamp, otherwise stop using the extract for cycle time.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Three independent defects each invalidate it on their own" overstates the SOP interval mismatch: it invalidates comparison to the SOP target but does not by itself invalidate a correctly defined receipt-to-release metric.

The claim that the catalog definition "decides whether any cycle-time metric is recoverable at all" is too absolute; an event log, decision audit trail, or reconciled snapshot could recover the metric even if qcore_release_ts is a load timestamp.
The assertion that the extract's disposition timestamp "fails" should remain conditional until the catalog definition or event log confirms timestamp semantics.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration could reflect a legitimate scheduled batch-disposition process rather than an interface load stamp; the apparent cutoff and HOLD pattern could also reflect a deliberately closed operational window. A catalog definition plus event-level timestamps and a coherent fresh extract would discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Avoid treating the catalog lookup as sufficient: explicitly request the timestamp definition together with one small event-level reconciliation sample linking QCore release, disposition/decision, and source-load times. This would distinguish a legitimate 02:10 batch process from an interface artifact and address snapshot inconsistency before KPI use.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Total apparent value across the 24 open requests... is USD 166,495.60"; "Every MTR-4401 donor is either at zero... or flagged reserved_for_critical_asset"; candidate table cites request IDs, donor IDs, quantities, revisions, and statuses.

The submission provides unusually specific row-level arithmetic and cross-file references, and distinguishes request evidence from inventory evidence. It does not, however, cite or discuss the global MaintStar snapshot freshness, limiting the completeness of the evidence chain.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Half the money is one part number that no search can unlock"; "Semantic search across the global catalog does not fix a planner not seeing their own bin"; "Identity cannot be confirmed for most of the money."

The analyst separates retrieval from transferability, local-stock visibility, identity, revision, and reservation mechanisms, and tests several competing explanations for apparent value. The reasoning is strong but treats inventory records as sufficiently current without testing temporal inconsistency.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "USD 28,980.72... actionable now, USD 55,789.64... needs engineering check, and USD 81,725.24... not transferable from current evidence"; "these are candidate matches only, never transfer recommendations"; "use the actionable band... as the ceiling, not the total."

Confidence is claim-specific and the candidate/engineering/not-transferable bands are useful bounds. However, labeling matches "Actionable now" is too strong without checking MaintStar freshness and point-in-time consistency; the submission gives no operational freshness adjustment or age threshold.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "The pilot is worth running, but the value case as framed is wrong"; "run the pilot as a candidate-surfacing tool with mandatory downstream gates"; "instrument it against realised transfers rather than search hits"; "Book no savings target from this sample."

This directly reframes the decision from savings realization to controlled candidate generation, protects against revision/UOM/qualification/reservation risks, and proposes measurement against realized transfers. It is a small, testable and operationally safer recommendation.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Half the money is one part number that no search can unlock"; "not a cross-site catalog problem at all"; "Better search would surface all four as hits and all four would still be declined."

The submission actively rejects the hypotheses that all apparent value is searchable cross-site supply or that better semantic search alone creates savings. It does not clearly state the strongest remaining competing interpretation or what future observation would revive it, particularly the possibility that stale extracts explain apparent stock and reservation conflicts.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "with mandatory downstream gates on reservation status, revision, UOM and receiving-site qualification"; no explicit prioritized request for a specific file, timestamp, owner interview, or discriminating next query.

The required checks are implied, but the analyst does not identify the smallest highest-value next evidence or explain how it would change the actionable band. A prioritized current MaintStar extract or timestamped inventory/reservation reconciliation is missing.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The "USD 28,980.72 actionable now" band is overstated unless inventory availability, reservations, and qualifications are confirmed against a fresh, coherent point-in-time source; the submission does not address MaintStar freshness or temporal inconsistency.

"Every MTR-4401 donor is either at zero or reserved" may be accurate in the cited extract, but the submission presents the resulting "not transferable" status without bounding the possibility that the extract is stale.

The statement that eleven requests represent "the true figure" for local stock visibility is directionally useful but should be labeled as extract-based apparent local coverage rather than current operational availability.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent donor pools, reservations, and local availability may reflect temporally inconsistent enterprise extracts rather than stable operational facts. Under that interpretation, semantic search could still generate valuable candidates, but both the USD 29k actionable ceiling and the USD 81.7k non-transferable classification require current reservation, stock, revision, and qualification confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a prioritized freshness-and-reconciliation step: obtain timestamped current MaintStar inventory plus reservation/criticality and qualification status for the high-value candidate donors, then recompute the actionable band and report how many candidates survive. This would directly test whether the claimed USD 29k ceiling is operationally real.
